content.title: About
content.content: Potato soup is a classic dish made from boiled or stewed potatoes, broth, vegetables, and seasonings. It has a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a creamy texture when the potatoes are mashed.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potatoes are the fourth most consumed food worldwide after rice, wheat, and corn.
Potato soup is popular in many cuisines: in Russia as "kartofelny sup", in France as "potage de pommes de terre", in Poland as "zupa ziemniaczana".
Potato soups are often prepared in colder months because they are warming and filling.
There are many variations: with cream, cheese, bacon, herbs, or carrots.
Potato soups can be clear broths or thick purées.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Potatoes provide vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and blood pressure.

items.title: Contains fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: When prepared without cream or butter, the soup is low in fat, making it suitable for light diets.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Adding too much salt can increase the risk of hypertension.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to potatoes.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Potatoes have a high glycemic index, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Solanine content
items.content: Green parts and sprouted tubers contain solanine, a toxin that should be avoided.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve potato soup hot, often garnished with herbs (parsley, dill), croutons, or grated cheese. Cream can be added for extra richness, and spices such as black pepper, paprika, or bay leaf enhance flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cooked soup in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. When frozen, it keeps for up to 2 months; thaw in the refrigerator before reheating.
